finding.text: The card "Proposed: when a card becomes a folder" (/live/design/page.jsonl line 125) says the folder name is "the card's existing id", but recursive-pages.md section 6 (Naming) says it is a slug of the title, "not its random id". Pick the title-slug rule (the owner's naming rule: slug = folder name, title separate) and correct the card.

recursive-pages.md section 6 says `apply_pages()` (page_tools.js:414) should check whether the target is an embedded card and promote it first. But apply_pages returns `why` at once when `at.target.length` is non-zero (page_tools.js:413: "`pages` works on the page itself, not inside a target"), so the proposed trigger has no hook there today. Say the target restriction must be relaxed, or name a different place for the check.

The brief asks for jsonl files, KB, deepest folder level and time to first render per url. The doc's section 7 table has only files and size, and the card has "last-req" instead of first render. The deepest level appears nowhere, and `/live/design/` and the sessions-day time are missing from the doc. Add the missing columns, or state they were not measured.

The task folder holds no measurement artifact (the probe script, or the raw request lists behind 168/118/31 files). The only record is the one session.jsonl line plus the cards, so a fresh agent cannot re-run or check the numbers. Add a small `measurements.md` or the probe script to the task folder and link it from the doc ("Load cost measurements for this task" currently links only the folder).

The `.jsonl` request count for `/live/` is 2 files and 3.7 KB. Section 7 and the cards do not say whether the 31-file synthetic check counts the 6 duplicate root re-fetches (37 requests, per the session log). Put "31 distinct, 37 requests" in the doc so the predicted-vs-network check is honest.

Nothing indexes the new sections. `core/Page/readme.md:82` links recursive-pages.md only as "every card a page you can open", with no mention that it now holds the load-cost measurements and the proposal. Update that line, and add the "break out / auto-upgrade" proposal to `doc/index-jsonl.md`, which section 7 links as the fix for wide folders. (Law 10)
The brief listed `LivePage`'s `save` as a possible folder path. The review confirms LivePage.js:84-92 only embeds a `live-screen` item, so the correction in the doc and card is right.

The 16 MB / "tens of seconds" extrapolation for 1000 flat children is linear from one measured day folder. The connection-cap reasoning is plausible but was not measured with a synthetic 1000-file tree, and the cards present it as a number.
The "no code change" fence held: the diff touches only recursive-pages.md. The task folder also holds `past-work.md` and `past-work/`, which belong to the indexing worker, not this task.
